description.narrative: Syftet med denna insats är att stärka och stödja det civila samhället, särskilt kvinnorganisationer, och HBTQ-grupper i Bolivia. Insatserna kommer att inriktas på att stärka gruppernas rättigheter, särskilt möjligheter till politiskt deltagande och inflytande, sexuella och reproduktiva rättigheter och kampen mot könsrelaterat våld, inklusive människohandel. For perioden 2022-2023
The purpose of this effort is focus on strengthening and support civil society organizations, especially women´s organizations and HBTQ groups in Bolivia. during the period 2022-2023

The General objective of Diakonias strategy: Contribute to the development of a strong and empowered civil society (SC), where diverse organizations and marginalized populations actively participate in local, departmental and/or national development and promote social and gender justice to eradicate inequalities.
The specific objective of this support is:
Secure the achieved results, end processes from the previous development and connect it to future processes by focusing on strengthening the partners, reviewing processes and resources and coordinating dialogue between civil society actors.

Bolivia has a regulatory body, based on the Political Constitution of the State (CPE), in which Art. 256 defines the preferential application of international human rights instruments. It also has institutions and mechanisms that promote the exercise of the rights of diverse women, young people, Afro-descendant and indigenous populations, and the LGBTIQ population. This regulatory body includes the bases for access to legal and safe abortion and for the exercise of rights of the LGBTIQ population. 2. There are organizations and networks that work on gender power relations from different angles and approaches, which constitutes an important potential for reflection, action and enforceability. 3. There is evidence of a Bolivian society that is increasingly alert to the need to transform relations between women and men, whose most dramatic testimony is violence against women. 4. Strengthened resurgence of actors such as youth, feminists, LGBTIQ and the recovery of spaces such as neighborhood and community groups, and urban-rural links that seek to address inequities in the country. 5. More and more indigenous women are empowering themselves, not only in the defense of their territories but also positioning their own agenda as women. 6. Mixed indigenous organizations more predisposed to support women's own claims. This support has function as a "Bridge" support to keep the partners business going until the Swedish Embassy will take a position on whether a larger support may be relevant in the future. The support has focus on the partners planned basic activities in order to be able to ensure a transition to a more sustainable phase of the support.
Achieved results 2022-2023
• Positioning of the Gender Committee of the Judicial Branch and Constitutional Court for the implementation of the Equal Opportunities Policy as an instance that promotes the integration of the gender perspective in the justice system and access to justice for women in situations of violence.
• The incorporation of the Constitutional Jurisdiction was achieved for the application of the Protocol for Judging with a Gender Perspective of the Judicial Body and the Protocol for Judging with a Gender and Intersectional Perspective, which reflects the progress of the integration of the gender perspective in the justice system.
• The strategy of the National Competition for Sentencing with a Gender Perspective (V version) is promoting changes in the justice system for the resolution of cases free of prejudices and gender stereotypes and based on the highest standards of human rights.
• Contributed to achieving substantial transformations in relation to the rights of the LGBTIQ population based on strategic litigation (started in 2021) and advocacy actions such as Amicus Curiae, which made it possible to have Constitutional Sentence 0577/2022-S2 through which , in the period of implementation of the bridge proposal, the free union of the first plaintiff couple was consolidated, also giving legal security to all the other unions that were made later and whose validity depended on this decision.
